business_problem: BBVA wanted to overhaul its mobile banking experience in Spain with faster performance, deeper personalization, easier day-to-day money management, and more proactive support for payments, savings and investing.
solution_summary: BBVA rebuilt its Spain mobile banking app on a single native code base that it says is scalable and exportable across the countries where the bank operates, then layered AI-driven experiences into that front end. The BBVA app is the primary delivery surface for wallet, card, Bizum and alert workflows, while Blue provides natural-language question answering inside the app. A new financial coach consumes customer income, expense, savings and loan data, performs an initial assessment, identifies improvement opportunities, and turns spending patterns into savings and cost-control recommendations, bill alerts and goal-setting prompts. Apple Intelligence is additionally integrated so eligible users can create personalized digital card designs for supported Visa cards on supported iPhones. The source does not disclose underlying models, storage services or back-end infrastructure, but it clearly describes an operational pipeline from banking data and customer habits to personalized in-app guidance and actions.

data_flow: Customer banking data including income, expenses, savings, loans, balances, bills and spending habits feeds the app’s AI features. The financial coach assesses that data, identifies improvement opportunities and returns savings goals, category-level cost controls and payment suggestions in the BBVA app, while Blue answers natural-language questions. The same app surface connects users to cards, the wallet and Bizum for immediate action.
business_outcome: BBVA reports a more personalized and faster mobile banking experience, AI-guided savings and expense control, direct access to cards and Bizum, proactive bill and overdraft support, and a mobile codebase that can scale to other countries where the bank operates.
